findings.recommendedModel: B2B2C-primary hybrid with a permanently-free direct student tier. Do NOT copy Copilot/Monarch ($95-199/yr paid subscription) — LOW WTP among ~6.0-6.5M Pell recipients (core need-based audience) makes a paid consumer subscription structurally mismatched. Rationale: (1) Freemium-to-paid conversion on mobile finance-adjacent apps sits at ~2-3%, so a paid tier for budget-constrained students converts far below even that; (2) the incumbent playbook for this population (campus financial wellness) is institutional licensing at $2-10/student/year across 600+ colleges via iGrad/Enrich — proven WTP that sits with the institution, not the student. Recommended: free forever for students (removes WTP barrier, matches low-touch/ambient design), monetized via (a) institutional per-student licenses to financial-aid offices and (b) optional low-price consumer 'Plus' tier for secondary higher-WTP subscription-heavy Gen Z segment.

institutionalChannel.pricingApproach: Per-enrolled-student annual license, $2-8/student/yr, tiered down as enrollment rises. Sold to financial-aid/student-success offices, not students. Position on outcome metrics (persistence, dropout reduction, disbursement stewardship) rather than app features.
institutionalChannel.evidence: iGrad/Enrich runs this exact model for the same student population — campus financial wellness quoted at $2-$10/student/yr based on enrollment, deployed at 600+ institutions, per-student price falling as enrollment grows. Establishes proven institutional WTP band for Pell/first-gen use cases. Our narrower single-purpose 'runway' tool should price at lower-to-mid end ($2-8) since it's a focused feature, not full curriculum.

unitEconomics.estimatedCAC: Direct-consumer CAC intentionally near-$0 (free tier, organic/campus-referral, ambient design). Institutional CAC is sales-led: multi-month sales cycles; ~$8k-$20k fully-loaded cost per closed institution, recovered across covered student base.
unitEconomics.estimatedARPPU: Direct 'Plus' ARPPU ~$18-24/yr, but applied to only low-single-digit % of free users (~2-3% freemium conversion, likely lower for primary audience), so blended direct ARPU well under $1/user/yr. Institutional 'ARPPU' is really ARPA: 10,000-student school at $3/student = ~$30k ARR; per-student economics ($2-8) dwarf realistic direct-consumer monetization.
unitEconomics.breakEvenLogic: A single mid-size campus contract (~10k students @ ~$3 = ~$30k ARR) covers more revenue than ~15,000+ free students would yield at ~2-3% conversion to ~$18/yr Plus (~$8k-9k). Break-even driven by institutional logos, not consumer conversion: at ~$8k-20k CAC per school and ~$30k ARR, payback inside year one, compounding via multi-year renewals. Consumer Plus is a margin add-on, not the break-even engine.

pricingLevers: Per-student enrollment tiering (steepen volume discounts for large/system-wide deals)
Multi-year/system (state university system) contracts for ACV expansion and lower churn
Outcome-based or at-risk pricing tied to persistence/retention lift
Bundling: unlock consumer Plus features free for institutionally-covered students
Sponsor/underwriter model (credit unions, banks, foundations subsidize per-student cost)
Data/reporting upsell: premium aggregate cohort analytics tier for institutional buyers
Consumer Plus price/packaging tests aimed only at higher-WTP Gen Z secondary segment
Free-year student promo (mirror YNAB) as conversion funnel into paid Plus post-graduation

sources.description: iGrad/Enrich campus financial wellness programs priced $2-$10/student/yr, enrollment-tiered; 600+ institutions
Freemium mobile app conversion benchmarks ~2-3% (median ~2.18% freemium vs ~12% hard paywall); RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps
Competitor consumer pricing anchors (YNAB $109/yr, Finny $1.99/mo, Copilot $95/yr, Monarch $99.99-199/yr, Cleo $5.99-14.99/mo)
RevenueCat subscription-app benchmarks: higher-priced apps show better Day-35 conversion; trial-to-paid exceeds freemium

gaps: No published direct WTP figure specific to Pell recipients for a budgeting app; LOW-WTP claim inherited from upstream, indirectly corroborated only.
iGrad/Enrich exact quote sheet not public (403 on pricing page); $2-10 band from aggregated search summaries, not verified rate card.
No finance-category-specific ARPU/conversion breakout retrievable; direct-tier estimates extrapolated from cross-category benchmarks.
Institutional CAC/sales-cycle estimate ($8k-20k) is industry-pattern assumption, not sourced data for this niche.
Unknown whether financial-aid offices pay for single-purpose tool vs only bundled full-curriculum suites — substitution risk with iGrad/Enrich.
